solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Novel, impenetrable, given to us

parts.note: something hard cannot be got through
The Times is the newspaper that hands this very puzzle to us

explanation.surface: A reviewer calls some novel impenetrable after it was handed over to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to us' is a self-reference: this puzzle comes from The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens wrote a novel with this title, set in the industrial town of Coketown.

clue.text: Husband with a meal ticket to get a sweetmeat

parts.note: LV is a luncheon voucher, a British meal ticket

explanation.surface: A man on a food voucher picks up a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: A luncheon voucher (LV) was a paper ticket British employers gave staff for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Halva is a Middle Eastern confection of sesame paste and sugar.

clue.text: Tigers run wild? Sounds about right

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A report of tigers running loose in a town seems plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that rings true seems believable and genuine.

clue.text: Investment secured, we hear, and set up with zero loss

indicators.note: we hear says the word for secured is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: trussed means tied up, secured

indicators.note: zero is the letter O, and loss says it is removed

parts.note: to found is to set up or establish

explanation.surface: Money tied up and established with no risk of losing a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust fund is money held in trust for someone, a kind of investment.

clue.text: Film depicting new detective's rise in force, say

indicators.note: in says the risen letters go inside the word for force

parts.note: might means strength or force

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector
to express is to say

explanation.surface: A movie showing a new police inspector climbing the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' reads upwards, giving IDN; 'in' splits the word for force after its first letter. 'depicting' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight Express is Alan Parker's 1978 film about a Turkish prison.

clue.text: He tunes fiddle, if discordant, for players

indicators.note: discordant means out of tune, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A musician tuning a violin badly enough to play out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like the musicians, but it is a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield United is an English football club, a team of players.

clue.text: Drunk unwilling to buy a round of drinks?

definitions.text: unwilling to buy a round of drinks?
definitions.meaning: stingy, mean with money, the kind who never stands a round

explanation.surface: A drinker who is plastered yet still never pays for the pub round.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both senses: inebriated, and miserly or close-fisted.

clue.text: Head in charge of subject

parts.note: the top is the head of something

explanation.surface: A department head responsible for one academic subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a matter under discussion, a subject.

clue.text: Author's work right superior to "King and I"

indicators.note: superior to means placed above, which in a down entry is before

parts.note: to go is to work or function
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A writer's work rated better than the musical The King and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorki was a Russian writer, author of The Lower Depths.

clue.text: Truants wandering round New York initially become unpleasant

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so the letters are moved around
initially takes the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Skiving pupils drifting around New York begin to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives NY, mixed in with TRUANTS by 'wandering'; 'round' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn nasty is to grow hostile or aggressive, an idiom.

clue.text: Weak local network? Good north of the border

parts.note: LAN is a local area network of computers
guid is the Scots form of good; north of the border means in Scotland

explanation.surface: A complaint that the local computer network is feeble, though a Scot says it is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of the border' is the British way of saying Scotland, where 'good' is spoken as GUID.
explanation.definitionFit: Languid means listless and lacking energy, so feeble or weak.

clue.text: Ruler in mood executed soldiers

indicators.note: executed means beheaded here, so the word for mood loses its head

parts.note: a temper is a state of mind or mood
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A tyrant in a foul humour has his troops put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like the ruler's deed, but it signals beheading: TEMPER loses its first letter to give EMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign ruler of an empire.

clue.text: A second class property

parts.note: a set is a class or group, as in a school set

explanation.surface: A description of a house as decent but second-rate real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something of value one owns, an item of property.

clue.text: Complaint among posh-sounding group?

parts.note: in means among, within

indicators.note: an upper-class accent turns the vowel of the clue's word for group toward an E sound

parts.note: a faction is a group within a party

explanation.surface: A grumble circulating among a clique of toffs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a cut-glass accent 'faction' comes out as 'fection', so 'in faction' becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or ailment, and an infection is one such.

clue.text: University dress mostly rejected in holiday island

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: An academic gown largely left behind on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts FROCK to FROC; 'rejected' turns U FROC round to give the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Spanish performers I catch doing cartwheel

parts.note: the cast is the group of performers in a show

indicators.note: doing a cartwheel turns head over heels, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: Spanish acrobats and I catch someone turning a cartwheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Castilian is standard Spanish, the language of Castile.

clue.text: Check on English artist beginning to rummage amongst his blessed rulers

indicators.note: amongst says the built letters go inside the word his

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the check comes last

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: beginning to picks just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A painter rummages through someone's belongings and checks on holy rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue means after, so the check goes last; 'amongst' splits 'his' after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarch is a chief priest or high church leader, so a ruler with sacred status.

clue.text: Large weapon beneath a cover, we're told, is part of early warning system?

indicators.note: beneath means placed below, which in a down entry is after

parts.note: an arm is a weapon

indicators.note: we're told says the word for cover is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: a caul is a membrane covering, as over a baby's head

explanation.surface: A big gun under camouflage forms part of a defence warning network.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm call warns of danger, and a wake-up call is an early warning, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Rider's state of health

definitions.meaning: a rider is a clause added to a contract, a stipulation
fitness or physical shape, as in being in good shape

explanation.surface: A jockey's fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stipulation in an agreement and one's physical state.

clue.text: Quickly peruse half of screed filling two pages

indicators.note: filling says the half-word goes inside the pages

parts.note: a spread is a pair of facing pages in a magazine

indicators.note: half of takes the latter three of the six letters of screed

explanation.surface: Skim a long piece of writing that runs across a double page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the back half of 'screed'; 'filling' needs a magazine spread, two facing pages, not PP.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed-read is to take in text very fast, skimming rather than studying.

clue.text: Trouble repulsed in Lyon, naturally

indicators.note: repulsed says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Of course there was unrest driven back in the French city of Lyon.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters YONNA sit inside 'Lyon, naturally', and 'repulsed' turns them back.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to bother or irritate them, a synonym.

clue.text: Golfing tournament participant is out

explanation.surface: A golfer in a major has been knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's oldest championship; a player in it is literally in The Open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out in public view is visible, not concealed, so not hidden.

clue.text: Guy the man sees from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means occasionally, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A fellow that the man meets now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man, but here it is the verb to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule or poke fun at them, so to tease.

clue.text: Cream topping for eclair with few calories

indicators.note: the topping of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: lite is a commercial spelling of light, low in calories

explanation.surface: A low-calorie topping of cream on a chocolate eclair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like the pastry filling, but means the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the select few at the top.

clue.text: Key European state

parts.note: main means key or chief

explanation.surface: A political note about a pivotal country in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA.

clue.text: Guardian leader penned by journalists was slightly moving?

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: ED is an editor; two of them make journalists plural

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial touched readers a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks emotional but means shifting position bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move gradually by small amounts, and the past tense fits 'was moving'.

clue.text: Number one drink in West

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in says the drink goes inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A chart-topping cocktail served in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like the definition, but 'Number' alone is the song (John Lennon's) and 'one' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or piece of music, and this is Lennon's famous track.

clue.text: Splitting pieces of granite

indicators.note: pieces of says the word is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock being cleaved into chunks of granite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing means ripping apart, so splitting into parts.

clue.text: Family member, German one, returning from Cologne after vacation

indicators.note: returning means the German word is read backwards

parts.note: ein is German for one

indicators.note: vacation means emptying, so Cologne is cleared of its middle letters, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A German relative comes home from Cologne after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the German for one round; 'after vacation' empties Cologne down to its two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a relative.

clue.text: Completely ignored single store in back rooms

indicators.note: in says the store and the one go inside the rooms
back means the word for rooms is read backwards

parts.note: dens are small private rooms
I is one, single
a deli is a food shop or store

explanation.surface: A lone shop tucked in back rooms gets no attention at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the rooms round to SNED, and 'in' places the single letter and the shop inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sidelined is to be pushed aside and left out of things.
